lines.en: Troy’s princess, Cassandra, wasn’t cruel to her soon-to-be sister-in-law, the legendary beauty Helen, out of spite.
lines.zh: 特洛伊的公主卡桑德拉对海伦——那位即将成为她嫂子的绝世美女——态度刻薄，并不是出于怨恨。

lines.en: It was because she was suffering under the weight of a tortuously twisted curse, which haunted her with appalling visions linked to Helen’s arrival.
lines.zh: 那是因为她正承受着一个无比阴毒的诅咒的重压：与海伦到来有关的种种可怕景象，不断纠缠着她。

lines.en: Helen was already married to the Spartan king Menelaus, after all.
lines.zh: 毕竟，海伦早已嫁给了斯巴达国王墨涅拉俄斯。

lines.en: And when Cassandra’s brother, Prince Paris, prepared to sail to Sparta, she foresaw his calamitous attachment to Helen and begged him to stay.
lines.zh: 当卡桑德拉的兄弟帕里斯王子准备启航前往斯巴达时，她预见到他对海伦的那段迷恋会带来灭顶之灾，于是恳求他留下来。

lines.en: But he’d merely dismissed her, fallen for Helen, and returned to Troy with her in tow.
lines.zh: 但他只是把她的劝告当作耳旁风，一头栽进了与海伦的恋情，还带着她一起回到了特洛伊。

lines.en: Beset by violent premonitions, Cassandra then warned that Menelaus’ vengeful crusade would lead to the brutal fall of their family and the city of Troy.
lines.zh: 被种种凶暴的预感缠身的卡桑德拉再次发出警告：墨涅拉俄斯的复仇之战，将导致他们的家族连同特洛伊城一起惨烈覆灭。

lines.en: But once again, people ignored her.
lines.zh: 可人们再一次无视了她。

lines.en: In fact, they always did.
lines.zh: 事实上，他们一贯如此。

lines.en: And this was the crux of her curse.
lines.zh: 而这，正是她那个诅咒的要害所在。

lines.en: As a young woman she had been pursued by the god Apollo.
lines.zh: 早在她还是个年轻女子的时候，阿波罗神就追求过她。

lines.en: He offered her the gift of prophecy.
lines.zh: 他把预知未来的能力当作礼物送给了她。

lines.en: But when she withdrew from his advances, he twisted his gift into a maddening hex: from that day on, Cassandra would be able to precisely see and describe the future— but her prophecies would never be believed.
lines.zh: 但当她退开身去、拒绝了他的亲近时，他把自己这份礼物扭曲成了一个令人发疯的恶咒：从那天起，卡桑德拉可以精确地看见并描述未来——但她的预言，永远不会被任何人相信。

lines.en: Despite this, Cassandra resolved to always speak the truth, even as her family fell deeper into denial.
lines.zh: 尽管如此，卡桑德拉依然下定决心，永远说出真相——哪怕她的家人越来越深地陷在不肯承认现实的泥潭里。

lines.en: Her dire warnings became increasingly repellent to her father, Trojan King Priam.
lines.zh: 她那些可怕的警告，让她的父亲、特洛伊王普里阿摩斯越来越反感。

lines.en: And when the war began, as she’d predicted, he declared that her meddling was bad for morale and confined her to a high tower.
lines.zh: 当战争如她所预言的那样打响时，国王宣称她的多嘴多舌会动摇军心，于是把她关进了一座高塔。

lines.en: From this unobstructed lookout, Cassandra watched everything unfold.
lines.zh: 从这个一览无余的瞭望处，卡桑德拉看着一切一步步地发生。

lines.en: Over 10 agonizing years, she witnessed her own grisly visions of senseless destruction come to pass on the battlefield below.
lines.zh: 在痛苦煎熬的十多年里，她亲眼看着自己那些关于无谓毁灭的可怖幻象，一一在下面的战场上应验。

lines.en: When dawn broke one day to reveal a huge wooden horse in place of the Greek encampment, the Trojans believed that the victory had finally been secured.
lines.zh: 有一天，黎明破晓时希腊人的营地不见了，取而代之的是一匹巨大的木马；特洛伊人以为，胜利终于到手了。

lines.en: Their enemies appeared to have fled, leaving this inscrutable token of peace behind.
lines.zh: 敌人看起来已经逃走，只留下这件说不清来路的和平信物。

lines.en: But as others streamed into the streets to celebrate, Cassandra realized the insidious truth.
lines.zh: 但当其他人涌上街头庆祝时，卡桑德拉看清了那个陰险的真相。

lines.en: Brandishing a battle-axe and a flaming torch, she descended from the tower and ran at the wooden horse, alerting everyone that it was a trick.
lines.zh: 她挥舞着战斧和燃烧的火把，从塔上冲下来，一路奔向那匹木马，大声提醒所有人：这是个骗局。

lines.en: Instead of heeding Cassandra’s warnings, they wrestled her to the ground and scoffed that she was getting more paranoid with age, then proceeded to tug the behemoth gift horse inside the city’s walls.
lines.zh: 人们不但没有理会卡桑德拉的警告，反而把她按倒在地，讥笑她真是年纪越大越疑神疑鬼，接着继续去拖那匹巨大的「礼物马」，把它拽进了城墙之内。

lines.en: As Troy fell into an oblivious slumber that night, Greek soldiers descended from the wooden horse's belly.
lines.zh: 那天夜里，特洛伊在毫无察觉中沉沉睡去，而希腊士兵从木马的肚子里爬了出来。

lines.en: All had gone according to plan, and they scattered among the city streets, intoxicated with their victory, to unleash a torrent of pent up, violent chaos.
lines.zh: 一切都在按计划进行。他们分散到城内的各条街道上，为即将到手的胜利而陶醉，准备释放出积压已久的、汹涌的暴力与混乱。

lines.en: Cassandra had seen her city burn and heard her people’s screams many times, but that didn't make the reality any easier to bear.
lines.zh: 卡桑德拉早已无数次看见自己的城市燃烧，听见同胞的惨叫，可这并没有让眼前的现实变得更容易承受。

lines.en: Her nightmare had come to pass.
lines.zh: 她的噩梦终究成真了。

lines.en: As dawn neared, the commander of the Greek army, Agamemnon himself, arrived to claim Cassandra as his prize.
lines.zh: 黎明将至时，希腊军队的统帅阿伽门农亲自前来，要把卡桑德拉当作自己的战利品带走。

lines.en: He dragged her back to his ship, boasting relentlessly of his victory as they set sail.
lines.zh: 他把她拖回自己的船上，一路启航时还在滔滔不绝地吹嘘自己的胜利。

lines.en: But Cassandra told him plainly that he'd be punished.
lines.zh: 但卡桑德拉直截了当地告诉他：他会受到惩罚。

lines.en: Earlier in the years of battle, Agamemnon had sacrificed his daughter to the war effort, hoping the gods would favor the Greeks in return.
lines.zh: 早在那几年征战之初，阿伽门农曾把自己的女儿献祭给了这场战事，指望众神会因此眷顾希腊人。

lines.en: Now Cassandra saw that his wife, Clytemnestra, awaited his return, poised for revenge.
lines.zh: 如今卡桑德拉看到，他的妻子克吕泰涅斯特拉正在家里等着他回去，随时准备复仇。

lines.en: But just as certainly as she saw that Agamemnon was sailing towards his own murder, Cassandra saw that she would also be killed in the fallout.
lines.zh: 但正如她确凿地看到阿伽门农正航向自己被谋害的结局一样，卡桑德拉同样清楚地看到：自己也会在这场灾祸中一同丧命。

lines.en: As always, she confronted the grim fate.
lines.zh: 一如既往，她直面了这个残酷的命运。

lines.en: In her lonely pact with the truth, no matter how ugly, Cassandra had always stood apart.
lines.zh: 在她与真相之间那份孤独的盟约里，无论真相多么丑陋，卡桑德拉始终一个人站在那里。

lines.en: After all, was it not her but everyone else who had fallen victim to the curse, living in deceit’s shadow, oblivious to reality until the bitter end?
lines.zh: 毕竟，真正沦为这个诅咒受害者的并不是她，而是其他所有人——他们活在欺骗的阴影里，直到苦涩的终局都对现实一无所知。
